subject: bug fix: too few digits of precision for double literal generation

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: bug fix: too few digits of precision for double literal generation
parts:
There's a bug in the way Stan is currently (v 1.1.0)
generating values for double literals (that is, doubles written
as numbers, not ones computed from other values).

I've patched the version in the git repository and of
course this fix will be in our next release (which this
bug motivates doing sooner rather than later).

Here are the details:

1. If you write a Stan program that does this:

int i;
real x;

x <- 1.0 / i;

stanc will generate the following C++ code:

int i;
double x;
x = 1 / i;

This is problematic because the C++ compiler interpets
(1 / i) as integer arithmetic, which rounds toward 0 (or
down on some platforms). The new version will generate:

int i;
double x;
x = 1.0 / i;

which will do the right thing.

In the interim, this problem can be coded around this very
ugly way:

transformed data {
real one;
...
one <- 1.0;
}
...
x = one / i;

2. If you have a long double literal, you will only get
seven decimal places of accuracy in the output.
That means, if you write this

x <- 1.2345678901234567890123456789;

the code that currently gets generated is:

x = 1.23457;

So I just changed our code generator to write out all decimals
to maximum precision (17 digits, according to Boost's
lexical_cast<string>(double)).

- Bob
